picks.editorial_note: A combined $1.175B commitment from Georgia Tech and Emory is one of the largest university AI investments to date, positioning the state as a national AI hub and signaling how seriously research universities are betting on AI infrastructure.
picks.title: Georgia Tech and Emory Invest More Than $1B in AI to Drive State’s Jobs, Economic Growth

picks.editorial_note: A White House-announced, 15-university regional supercomputing consortium marks a significant federal push to coordinate AI compute capacity across academia, with implications for national AI research strategy.
picks.title: UK partners with regional universities in super intelligence computing consortium

picks.editorial_note: SLAC's DOE Genesis Mission award applies autonomous AI-driven discovery to catalysis research, a concrete step toward AI systems that can independently design and run scientific experiments.
picks.title: SLAC to lead a Department of Energy Genesis Mission project for Super Intelligence (SI)-driven autonomous discovery in catalysis

picks.editorial_note: Phase II DOE funding for Berkeley Lab's MOAT-Core project shows sustained federal investment in applying AI to particle accelerator design, advancing a key tool for fundamental physics research.
picks.title: Super Intelligence for Particle Accelerators Gets Another Boost

picks.editorial_note: Georgia Tech's Nexus supercomputer, backed by $20M in NSF funding and built with University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, opens major AI compute capacity to researchers nationwide — expanding access beyond well-resourced institutions.
picks.title: Georgia Tech Opens Supercomputer to Researchers Nationwide

picks.editorial_note: SLAC's SPIRE project aims to build fully autonomous self-driving laboratories where AI agents and robots run photon-science experiments independently, a notable step toward automating the scientific method itself.
picks.title: SLAC leads new project to build the self-driving laboratory of the future

picks.editorial_note: Fermilab's two Genesis Mission awards apply AI to microelectronics and quantum information science design, pairing national lab expertise with cutting-edge chip and quantum research.
picks.title: Fermilab to lead two new Genesis Mission awards to accelerate development of microelectronics and quantum

picks.editorial_note: A CWRU alumnus's optical computing chips, which use light instead of electricity to run AI workloads, target one of AI's most pressing constraints — energy consumption — with real commercial backing via his startup Neurophos.
picks.title: A CWRU entrepreneur studied invisibility cloaks. Now he’s working to cut AI’s energy use | CWRU Newsroom | Case Western Reserve University

picks.editorial_note: An NIH Director's Pioneer Award of roughly $6 million will fund an AI-human discovery engine using LLM agents to generate and test cancer hypotheses, a prestigious recognition of AI's growing role in biomedical research.
picks.title: Dr. Olivier Elemento Wins NIH Director’s Pioneer Award
picks.university: Weill Medical College of Cornell University

picks.editorial_note: TUM spinout RobCo reaching unicorn status with plug-and-play industrial robotics demonstrates strong commercial validation of university-born AI/robotics research reaching billion-euro market scale.
picks.title: RobCo: TUM’s 24th unicorn
